result.topic_en: Concluding remarks of a treatise on the expansion of expressions of the form α/√(β+γcosφ), announcing a more general demonstration and methods for all coefficients, and noting their usefulness in the theory of planetary perturbations.

methods.what: Reduction of the expression to the standard form α/√(β+γcosφ) by the substitution φ = 2ψ
methods.quote:
enim functiones reducentur ad formam $\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{(\beta-\gamma+2\gamma\cos\psi^2)}}$, ei de

methods.what: Corollary: expressions α/√(β+γcosφ) with equal extreme (max/min) values have equal constant terms in their Fourier expansion
methods.quote:
si plures expressiones
tales $\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{(\beta+\gamma\cos\varphi)}}$ ita comparatae sint, ut ipsarum valores
extremi aequales sint: terminos constantes ex ipsarum evolutione
prodeuntes necessario aequales fieri, etiamsi omnes reliqui coëffi-
cientes valde discrepent.

items.quote:
in sequentibus demonstrationem

items.english: in what follows a much more general demonstration of the same theorems, from more genuine principles, will be given

items.quote:
praetereaque mox etiam omnes reliquos
coëfficientes Q, R, S etc. per methodos aeque expeditas eruere do-
cebimus
items.english: and besides we shall soon also teach how to derive all the remaining coefficients Q, R, S etc. by equally expeditious methods

items.quote:
Quantae enim utilitatis sit evolutio coëfficientium P, Q, R, S etc.
tam rapida, ut ea quae ex his principiis promanat, in astro-
nomia physica sive theoria perturbationum planetarum, nemo
ignorat.
items.english: For no one is unaware of how useful so rapid an evaluation of the coefficients P, Q, R, S etc., such as flows from these principles, is in physical astronomy or the theory of planetary perturbations.

Moreover it follows immediately from the preceding that if several such expressions have equal extreme values, the constant terms of their expansions are necessarily equal, even if all the other coefficients differ greatly.
